page: The Microsoft Azure M32dms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It runs on a dedicated Intel Xeon 8473C processor using the x86_64 architecture, providing 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at up to 4.0 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation stands at 875.0 GB of RAM, equating to 27.34 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with 1100 GB of bundled local SSD storage and features no dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results place the M32dms_v2 in the middle tier for multi-threaded compute, scoring 23015.93 in stress-ng multi-core tests, 12524.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 33529.95 in PassMark CPU tests. Single-core performance is more constrained, registering 1406.19 on stress-ng, reflecting a weak rating compared to compute-centric offerings. Synthetic memory testing yielded a PassMark memory score of 1422.63, while database operations reached 12655.71 on PassMark and achieved 28.81 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the instance trades peak single-thread execution speed for an exceptionally high memory footprint and bundled local SSD capacity. Workloads requiring vast in-memory caching, large transactional databases, enterprise relational database management systems, and high-capacity analytics pipelines benefit most from this density profile.
description: Microsoft Azure M32dms_v2 is a memory-optimized cloud server engineered for large-scale enterprise workloads and database environments. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8473C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 16 physical cores, 32 vCPUs at up to 4.0 GHz, and a substantial 105 MB L3 cache. It features an expansive 875.0 GB of system memory, yielding 27.34 GB per vCPU, alongside 1100 GB of bundled local SSD storage without GPU acceleration. Across synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates average multi-core processing throughput, recorded at 12524.0 on Geekbench and 33529.95 on PassMark CPU, while achieving 28.81 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. Single-core execution reflects lower relative throughput. This hardware profile makes the M32dms_v2 well matched for memory-intensive applications, including in-memory relational databases, enterprise transactional engines, Redis caching tiers, and large data processing pipelines requiring substantial memory capacity per thread.
